An unsupported registration request can log a node out, consume a pre-auth key or start a login before its version is rejected. Enforce the capability floor before those effects occur.

title: hscontrol: use the node-key index for DERP admission
body:
Every DERP client-verification request scans the entire node list, making connection admission more expensive as the tailnet grows. Use the existing node-key index while preserving admission for registered nodes.

> Generated with the help of an AI assistant

title: state: persist resolved node names during registration
body:
New registrations commit a seed DNS name before collision and fallback handling, so headscale restarts can restore duplicate or empty names. Resolve and persist the final name in the serialized node-store creation path, committing node creation and single-use key consumption before publishing the node. Failed creation leaves the node unpublished and the key available for retry.

> Generated with the help of an AI assistant

title: mapper: retain the logtail instruction across client restarts
body:
Clients forget the logtail instruction when their process restarts, allowing uploads despite `logtail.enabled: false`. Every opening full map, including the expired-node response, must carry that instruction; clients with `data-plane-audit-logs` stay down until `tailscale up`.

> Generated with the help of an AI assistant

title: mapper: preserve node pings when a full update is queued
body:
A full map update can discard a pending node ping, leaving the caller waiting for an answer that never arrives. Preserve targeted pings across the collapse to a full update.

> Generated with the help of an AI assistant

title: servertest: wait for stable via-route netmaps before comparison
body:
Peer counts can converge before route approvals, primary selection and packet filters reach clients, making via-route compatibility tests fail prematurely. Require the complete netmap comparison to hold across consecutive ticks so transient matches cannot hide later drift.

> Generated with the help of an AI assistant

title: state: revalidate pre-auth key reuse when registration applies
body:
A node can expire or change its node key while re-registration waits for the NodeStore writer, making an earlier decision to permit an invalid pre-auth key stale. Decide whether reuse is allowed against the node and time at the point of mutation.

title: noise: prevent SSH check verdict replay from approving access
body:
Reading a consumed SSH authentication channel yields a zero verdict that is treated as approval, even after rejection. A repeated follow-up must receive a fresh policy decision instead of implicit approval.

title: mapper: retain reconnect peer removals until delivery
body:
A full update or another disconnect can discard a queued reconnect removal after the peer baseline has already been reset. Keep those peers tracked until the removal reaches the client, so a later full update or reconnect can recover it.

title: util: parse "0o"-prefixed file modes in GetFileMode
body:
## Description

The viper default for `unix_socket_permission` is `"0o770"`, but `GetFileMode`
parses the value with `strconv.ParseUint` using base 8, which rejects the
Go-style `0o` prefix — only base 0 accepts it. The parse fails and the function
silently falls back to `PermissionFallback` (`0700`), so with
`unix_socket_permission` unset, the unix socket is created with mode `0700` and
is never group-accessible, even though both the default and
`config-example.yaml` (which spells the same value unprefixed, `"0770"`)
clearly intend `0770`.

The existing tests in `cmd/headscale/headscale_test.go` load
`config-example.yaml` (where the key is `"0770"`), so the default-value path
had no coverage and the mismatch went unnoticed.

This trims the `0o` prefix before parsing, so `"0o770"`, `"770"` and `"0770"`
all parse as octal 770. `TestGetFileMode` covers the accepted spellings
(`770`, `0770`, `0o770`, `0o700`) plus the invalid/empty fallback cases.
Verified with `go test ./hscontrol/util/` and the config-loading tests in
`cmd/headscale`.

Found while diagnosing why a sandboxed root systemd service (empty
`CapabilityBoundingSet`, so no `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE`) running with the `headscale`
supplementary group got `permission denied` on `/run/headscale/headscale.sock`
(`srwx------ headscale:headscale`) on a NixOS host running 0.29.3 with
`unix_socket_permission` unset.

## Checklist

- [x] have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) file
- [ ] raised a GitHub issue or discussed it on the projects chat beforehand (bug fix, open to contributions without discussion per CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] added unit tests
- [ ] added integration tests (pure string-to-FileMode function; unit coverage is sufficient)
- [x] updated documentation if needed (no doc change: the intended mode 0770 is unchanged)
- [x] updated CHANGELOG.md

title: [Bug] unix_socket_permission default "0o770" is not parsed, silently falls back to 0700
body:
## Is this a support request?

- [x] This is not a support request

## Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

## Current Behavior

With `unix_socket_permission` unset, the unix socket is created with mode `0700`, so it is not accessible to the `headscale` group — despite the intended default of `0770`.

Root cause:

- `hscontrol/types/config.go` sets the viper default to `"0o770"` (Go-style octal literal spelling),
- but `hscontrol/util`'s `GetFileMode` parses the string with `strconv.ParseUint(s, 8, 64)`, and base 8 rejects the `0o` prefix (only base 0 accepts it),
- so the parse fails and the function silently falls back to `PermissionFallback` (`0700`).

The existing tests in `cmd/headscale/headscale_test.go` load `config-example.yaml`, where the key is the unprefixed `"0770"`, so the default-value path has no coverage.

## Expected Behavior

The default resolves to mode `0770` (group-accessible), as both the default value and `config-example.yaml` ("0770") clearly intend.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Run headscale with `unix_socket_permission` absent from the configuration file (the default value path — note `config-example.yaml` sets the key explicitly to `"0770"`, which is why following the example verbatim hides this).
2. `ls -l /var/run/headscale/headscale.sock` → `srwx------` (expected `srwxrwx---`).

Minimal parse demo:

```go
strconv.ParseUint("0o770", 8, 64) // error: invalid syntax
strconv.ParseUint("0o770", 0, 64) // 504 (0o770), ok
strconv.ParseUint("0770", 8, 64)  // 504, ok (why the example config works)
```

## Environment

- OS: NixOS
- Headscale version: 0.29.3
- Tailscale version: n/a (server-side)

## Debug information

- Headscale configuration: the `unix_socket_permission` key is absent from the config file, so the value in effect is the viper default `"0o770"` — exactly the path that misbehaves.
- Socket observed on the affected host: `srwx------ headscale:headscale /run/headscale/headscale.sock` (NixOS module path).
- Impact example: a sandboxed root systemd service (empty `CapabilityBoundingSet`, so no `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE`) running with the `headscale` supplementary group gets `permission denied` connecting to the socket — the documented group access path (nixpkgs sets `RuntimeDirectoryMode=0750` for exactly this) does not work with the default.
- Netmap dumps / policy / trace logs: n/a — deterministic server-side string-parsing bug, fully covered by the demo above.
- Proposed fix (one line, trim the `0o` prefix before parsing) along with `TestGetFileMode` was in #3528, auto-closed by the vouch gate. Happy to reopen on request, or re-submit once acknowledged.

title: state: send relogin of an expired node as a whole node
body:
## Why

- I'm using OIDC flow for our VPN and users are required by policy to
  use 2FA every time they connect after some time. So I use expiration
  on their clients that forces them to go through OIDC login flow again
  where I can enforce any MFA/password policy we require.
- The issue is that when user reauthenticates itself, their traffic does
  not go through tailnet until they restart tailscaled.

## Problem

- After a node's key expires and the user re-authenticates (web/OIDC
  `tailscale up`, or a pre-auth key), the node gets a new node key and
  reaches Running, but peers drop all its WireGuard traffic.
- Disco keeps working (`tailscale ping` gets pongs, peers log `now using`),
  but TSMP/ICMP time out and `LastHandshake` stays zero.
- It recovers only after `tailscaled` restarts on the node, or Headscale
  restarts.

## Cause

- Peers get the expired node as a whole node with `Expired: true`.
- The relogin goes out as `change.NodeKeyRotated`, a `tailcfg.PeerChange`
  patch (Key, DiscoKey, KeyExpiry, Endpoints).
- `PeerChange` has no `Expired` field, and the client's patch path leaves
  it as it is, so peers keep the node expired.
- The Tailscale client gives an expired peer no AllowedIPs
  (`routemanager.peerViewOf`), so wireguard-go does not create the lazy
  peer and drops its handshakes.
- Why it doesn't happen on every relogin: if the first MapRequest after
  the relogin changes peer-visible Hostinfo, `buildMapRequestChangeResponse`
  sends the whole node anyway and the flag clears. This is what happens
  when the client registers without its peerapi services and adds them
  once Running.
- It shows up when the expired client has settled before the user logs
  in again: it keeps its netmap and serves peerapi again while in
  NeedsLogin (seen with 1.98 and newer; not with 1.84), so it registers
  with the same Hostinfo it later reports, and nothing ever clears the
  flag.

## Fix

- `reauthChange` now gets `wasExpired`. If the node was expired before
  the relogin, the relogin is sent as `change.NodeAdded` instead of the
  key-rotation patch.
- This covers both `HandleNodeFromAuthPath` and `HandleNodeFromPreAuthKey`.
- Relogins of non-expired nodes keep the patch path.
- I checked the other paths that can make a node non-expired:
  `SetNodeExpiry` and new registrations already send the whole node, and
  a MapRequest can't change expiry.
- Fix was co-authored with LLM, hand checked by me.

## Tests

All of these fail without the fix and pass with it:

- Integration: `TestAuthWebFlowReloginExpiredNode`. For each client, it
  expires one node, waits until the client is in NeedsLogin with peerapi
  serving again, then logs it back in via the web flow. It checks that
  every peer sees the new key with `Expired=false` and gets a TSMP pong
  from it. Clients older than 1.98 are skipped as the relogged node
  because they don't serve peerapi while expired, so their relogin always
  changes Hostinfo; they still take part as peers.
  - Without the fix: 1.102, 1.98, head and unstable fail on the expired
    flag and the TSMP ping.
- servertest: `TestReloginOfExpiredNodeClearsPeerExpiry`. A deterministic
  version using a real `controlclient.Direct` with fixed Hostinfo.
- `TestHandleNodeFromAuthPath_ReloginOfExpiredNode`: the interactive path
  returns a whole-node change when the node was expired, and a patch when
  it was not.
- `TestReauthChange` extended with the expired case.

---

- [x] have read the CONTRIBUTING.md file
- [ ] raised a GitHub issue or discussed it on the projects chat beforehand
- [x] added unit tests
- [x] added integration tests
- [ ] updated documentation if needed  <!-- not needed -->
- [x] updated CHANGELOG.md

title: [Bug] Peers keep dropping traffic from a node that re-authenticates after its key expired
body:
### Is this a support request?

- [x] This is not a support request

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Current Behavior

- I'm using the OIDC flow for our VPN, and by policy users have to go through 2FA again after some time. So I set an expiry on their nodes, which forces them through the OIDC login flow again, where I can enforce our MFA/password policy.
- The problem: when the user re-authenticates, the node gets a new node key and reaches Running, but its traffic does not go through the tailnet until they restart `tailscaled`.
  - disco works: `tailscale ping` gets pongs and the peers log `now using …`
  - TSMP and ICMP time out, and `LastHandshake` stays zero on both sides
  - on the peers, the node shows the new key but `Expired: true`
- Restarting Headscale also fixes it.
- With expiry as a policy, this hits basically every relogin. The client sits in NeedsLogin until the user logs in again, which is exactly the condition that triggers the bug (see Steps To
Reproduce).

### Expected Behavior

- After re-authentication, peers see the node with its new key and `Expired: false`, and traffic flows without restarting anything.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Two connected user-owned nodes A and B, with Tailscale 1.98 or newer on A.
2. Expire A: `headscale nodes expire --identifier <A>`.
3. Wait until A sits in NeedsLogin and serves peerapi again, i.e. `tailscale status --json | jq .Self.PeerAPIURL` on A is not empty. This takes about a second.
4. Log A back in via the web flow: `tailscale up`, then `headscale auth register --auth-id …`. OIDC behaves the same.
5. On B, `tailscale status --json` shows A with the new key and `Expired: true`, and `tailscale ping --tsmp <A>` times out.

Step 3 matters. If A logs in before it settles, it registers without its peerapi services and adds them once Running. Headscale then sends the whole node because peer-visible Hostinfo changed, and that hides the bug. A user who comes back after their node expired always logs in from the settled state.

Automated reproduction is in https://github.com/nextsux/headscale/tree/fix/reauth-expired-full-node:
- `TestAuthWebFlowReloginExpiredNode` (integration): on current main, 1.102, 1.98, head and unstable fail on the expired flag and on the TSMP ping.
- `TestReloginOfExpiredNodeClearsPeerExpiry` (servertest): deterministic, without Docker.

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Debian 13 (Headscale, VM with systemd); Arch Linux (client)
- Headscale version: 0.29.4; the relevant code is unchanged on main
- Tailscale version: 1.102.4 on the client
- Number of nodes: ~50; OIDC login; ACLs with `autogroup:self` plus routes
```

### Runtime environment

- [x] Headscale is behind a (reverse) proxy
- [ ] Headscale runs in a container

### Debug information

Cause:
- Peers receive the expired node as a whole node with `Expired: true`.
- On relogin, `reauthChange` sends `change.NodeKeyRotated`, a `tailcfg.PeerChange` patch (Key, DiscoKey, KeyExpiry, Endpoints).
- `PeerChange` has no `Expired` field. The `tailcfg.Node.Expired` docs say: "Control may send this; clients are only allowed to set this from false to true." So only a whole node from
control can clear it, and the patch leaves peers with `Expired: true`.
- The client then gives the peer no AllowedIPs, so wireguard-go drops its handshakes.
- The comment on `NodeKeyRotated` says the KeyExpiry zero value un-expires the peer. It only clears the timestamp, not `Expired`.

Proposed fix: send the relogin of a node that was expired as a whole node (`change.NodeAdded`). Branch: https://github.com/nextsux/headscale/tree/fix/reauth-expired-full-node; it was opened as #3530 and auto-closed by the vouch gate. Fix was co-authored with LLM, hand checked by me.

<details><summary>Headscale trace log around the relogin (integration test, node 3, client 1.98)</summary>

```
2026-10-03T13:55:21Z INF Updating existing node registration via reauth existing={"node.expired":true,"node.id":3,"node.key":"[nGgMb]",...}
2026-10-03T13:55:22Z TRC classified MapRequest ... disco_key.changed=true hostinfo.changed=true hostinfo.peer_changed=false key.changed=false node.id=3 ... type=patch
2026-10-03T13:55:22Z INF node connected node.expired=false node.id=3 node.key=[z31rO] node.online=true
2026-10-03T13:55:22Z TRC classified MapRequest ... hostinfo.changed=true hostinfo.peer_changed=false node.id=3 ... type=empty
2026-10-03T13:55:23Z DBG node change processing started node.id=3 reason="node key rotated (relogin)"
2026-10-03T13:55:23Z DBG node change processing started node.id=3 reason="node online"
```
No `node added` for node 3 follows. The next ones, at 13:55:53, are the following subtest expiring node 6.
</details>

<details><summary>Map responses received by peer node 1 about node 3</summary>

```json
{"file":"13-55-11.306","PeersChanged":[{"ID":3,"Key":"nodekey:9c680c6d…","Expired":true,"KeyExpiry":"2026-10-03T13:55:07.352987208Z"}]}
{"file":"13-55-12.107","PeersChangedPatch":[{"NodeID":3,"Online":false}]}
{"file":"13-55-22.507","PeersChangedPatch":[{"NodeID":3,"Endpoints":["172.18.0.7:36294"],"Key":"nodekey:cf7d6b3a…"}]}
{"file":"13-55-23.306","PeersChangedPatch":[{"NodeID":3,"Endpoints":["172.18.0.7:36294"],"Key":"nodekey:cf7d6b3a…","DiscoKey":"discokey:feb8d070…"}]}
{"file":"13-55-23.307","PeersChangedPatch":[{"NodeID":3,"Online":true}]}
```
</details>

<details><summary>Test failure without the fix</summary>

```
command stdout: ping "100.64.0.4" timed out        (repeats 13:55:23 – 13:55:51)
Error:      Should be false
Messages:   peer must clear the expired flag
Error:      Received unexpected error: command failed, stderr: no reply
Error:      "ping \"100.64.0.4\" timed out\n" does not contain "pong"
Test:       TestAuthWebFlowReloginExpiredNode/ts-75a4fc-1-98-d6bf61
Messages:   peer must reach the relogged node over WireGuard
```
</details>

title: [Bug] Exit nodes receive WireGuard packets but don't forward traffic
body:
### Is this a support request?

- [x] This is not a support request

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Current Behavior

Exit nodes appear in clients and show as "active", but no traffic flows through them. Selecting an exit node blackholes all internet traffic (curl times out, pages don't load).

### Expected Behavior

Traffic should flow through exit nodes.

This worked fine on Tailscale SaaS with the same hosts and clients. Issue started after migrating to Headscale.


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set up Headscale v0.29.4
2. Register Linux node, advertise exit routes, approve them
3. From macOS or Linux client, select the exit node
4. Run `curl -sI --max-time 10 https://google.com` → times out after 10s
5. On exit node, `tcpdump -i any udp port 41641` shows packets arriving from client, but traffic doesn't flow

### Environment

```markdown
- Headscale version: v0.29.4 (upgraded from v0.29.3, issue persists on both)
- Tailscale versions: v1.102.4 on all nodes (Mac, KDE Linux desktop, exit node hosts)
- Network: All clients on same LAN (192.168.1.x)
```

### Runtime environment

- [x] Headscale is behind a (reverse) proxy
- [x] Headscale runs in a container

### Debug information

### Headscale control plane
- Exit node routes approved: `headscale nodes list-routes` shows `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` as Approved/Available/Serving for both nodes
- No errors in `docker logs headscale` related to exit nodes, routes, filters, or ACL
- Node registration succeeds, map updates return 200
- DERP configured (using Tailscale's public DERP map)

### Exit node host config
- `net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1`
- iptables `ts-postrouting` has MASQUERADE rule for mark `0x40000/0xff0000`
- iptables `FORWARD` chain accepts via `ts-forward`
- Host itself reaches internet fine (curl shows Tokyo IP via Mullvad)
- Tailscale listening on UDP 41641

### Client config
- `tailscale status` shows exit node as `active; exit node; direct 192.168.1.80:41641`
- macOS routing table shows `default` via `utun10` (Tailscale interface)
- Full Tailscale app restart done (not just CLI down/up)
- Tested from both macOS and Linux (KDE) clients — both fail identically
- Tested both exit nodes — both fail identically

### ACL policy
- Policy passes `headscale policy check`
- Contains: `{"action": "accept", "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["*:*"]}`
- Should allow all traffic, including exit node forwarding

## Key evidence: packets arrive but vanish

**tcpdump on exit node (raw WireGuard UDP):**
```
sudo timeout 15 tcpdump -i any udp port 41641 -c 20
```
Shows bidirectional UDP between client (192.168.1.15) and exit node (192.168.1.80:41641), including large data packets (1168, 1312 bytes) when client runs `curl` via exit node. WireGuard handshake succeeds, data packets arrive.

**tcpdump on exit node (decrypted tailscale0):**
```
sudo timeout 15 tcpdump -ni tailscale0 'host 100.100.0.22 and tcp'
```
Shows **nothing** when client curls via exit node. (Note: forwarded packets may bypass tailscale0 interface, so this alone isn't conclusive.)

**iptables counters:**
- `FORWARD` chain shows traffic, but counters don't clearly correlate with exit node tests
- `ts-postrouting` MASQUERADE has matched packets, but unclear if from our tests

## Home Assistant reproduction

A clean Home Assistant node (Tailscale add-on) was registered and tested as an exit node. It reproduced the **blackhole**: selectable as exit node, client traffic times out, no forwarding.

## Ruled out: #2469 (restrictive per-user ACL)

Upstream issue [#2469](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/issues/2469) describes identical symptoms (exit node selectable but traffic blackholes), but its root cause was restrictive per-user ACLs (`user1 → user1:*` only, blocking cross-user exit node traffic).

That does not apply here. This deployment's policy contains:

```json
{"action": "accept", "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["*:*"]}
```

All clients and exit nodes are owned by the same user (`autogroup:member`), and the policy allows all traffic. `headscale policy check` passes. The ACL is not the blocker.

## Ruled out: #3087 (`autogroup:internet` grant)

Upstream issue [#3087](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/issues/3087) found that in Headscale 0.27/0.28, exit-node traffic only flowed with an explicit `autogroup:internet` grant — the docs' host-based restriction method broke (exit nodes visible but no traffic).

Tested both syntaxes on v0.29.4, neither fixed it:

1. **ACLs syntax** — added `{"action": "accept", "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["autogroup:internet:*"]}` to `acls`. Deployed, selected exit node, `curl` timed out.
2. **Grants syntax** — added `"grants": [{"src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["autogroup:internet"], "ip": ["*"]}]` alongside the existing `acls` (OR logic, additive). `headscale policy check` passed, deployed, selected exit node, `curl` timed out.

The official docs ([headscale.net/stable/ref/routes/](https://headscale.net/stable/ref/routes/)) use `grants` syntax for all exit-node examples and describe `autogroup:internet` as the mechanism. Neither syntax unblocks traffic on v0.29.4. The ACL/filter layer is not the cause.

## What was tried
1. Verified IP forwarding, NAT, firewall on exit nodes
2. Restarted Tailscale on clients (full app restart on macOS)
3. Deleted and re-registered exit node with fresh keys (`headscale nodes delete`, `tailscale logout`, fresh `tailscale up --force-reauth`)
4. Re-approved routes after re-registration
5. Upgraded Headscale v0.29.3 → v0.29.4 (v0.29.4 includes fix for "exit nodes not offered by recent macOS/iOS clients" #3487, but didn't help)
6. Verified DERP configuration
7. Checked Headscale logs (no errors)
8. Tested main-eeaac68 (includes #3493 fixes: 61d1599, 7efd22d), issue persists.

title: fix(poll): never delete an online node
body:
Hi, thanks for the awesome project, i have been a happy user for awhile, using this for both my personal tsnet, as well as some other projects i maintain or am involved in.

I ran into a very rare race condition where a node tried reconnecting as headscale was handling the disconnect, causing the GC to be scheduled even thought the node reconnected and was healthy.  Unfortunately, the GC would delete the node, which caused the client to get in a unhealthy state.  Its a very, very short window this could happen, i was just unlucky enough to run into it.

The exact sequence for this to happen:

1. The old session marks it offline.
2. The new session marks it online and cancels the GC timer.
3. The old session then arms the timer.

The node is still online, but it gets deleted when the timer fires.

Related PR's that helped with similar race conditions, but does not quite protect against this.

- #3298 drops a deletion whose timer was cancelled.
- #3308 stops overlapping sessions from marking a node offline.
- #3383 cancels the timer only after Connect.

This PR has 2 changes:
1. Don't arm a timer for a node that is back online
2. Never delete an online node (failsafe for possible other conditions not identified yet)

Also includes tests.

title: [Bug] Healthy node gets deleted due to race condition.
body:
### Is this a support request?

- [x] This is not a support request

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Current Behavior

Hi, thanks for the awesome project, i have been a happy user for awhile, using this for both my personal tsnet, as well as some other projects i maintain or am involved in.

I ran into a very rare race condition where a node tried reconnecting as headscale was handling the disconnect, causing the GC to be scheduled even thought the node reconnected and was healthy. Unfortunately, the GC would delete the node, which caused the client to get in a unhealthy state. Its a very, very short window this could happen, i was just unlucky enough to run into it.

Related PR's that helped with similar race conditions, but does not quite protect against this.

#3298 drops a deletion whose timer was cancelled.
#3308 stops overlapping sessions from marking a node offline.
#3383 cancels the timer only after Connect.

I have a PR to address this, see #3534

### Expected Behavior

We should not schedule the GC to delete a node, and a healthy node should never be deleted 

### Steps To Reproduce

The exact sequence for this to happen:

1. The old session marks it offline.
2. The new session marks it online and cancels the GC timer.
3. The old session then arms the timer.
4. The node is still online, but it gets deleted when the timer fires.

To reproduce: 
1. Connect an node.
2. Drop its connection for just over 10 seconds, so the reconnect grace ends.
3. Have it reconnect while the old session is between Disconnect and afterServeLongPoll. That window is only a few milliseconds, and things like database latency could affect the timing. 

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Debian Linux on Kubernetes
- Headscale version: v0.29.4
- Tailscale version: v1.100.0
```

### Runtime environment

- [ ] Headscale is behind a (reverse) proxy
- [x] Headscale runs in a container

### Debug information

The client is a custom Go binary using the tnset library, i don't have the logs there anymore.

title: policy/v2: skip via resolution when the policy has no via grants
body:
What happened:
- After upgrading to 0.29, we run about 450 nodes, and headscale saturated an 8 vCPU host every weekday.
- A CPU profile put 82% of CPU in buildTailPeers → RoutesForPeer → ViaRoutesForPeer → AutoGroup.Resolve.
- Our policy has no via grants at all.

What the function does:
- It is called once per peer in every map response.
- It converts every ACL to grants, one grant per destination, and resolves every grant's sources and destinations against all nodes.
- Only then does it check Via.
- Without a via grant the result is always empty, so all of that work is discarded.

Commit 1: the fix
- Return early if no grant in pol.Grants has via.
- The result is guaranteed unchanged: only via grants add to it, and ACLs can't carry via (aclToGrants never sets it).
- Benchmarks:

| Policy, 1,000 nodes | Before    | After                |
|---------------------|-----------|----------------------|
| ACL-only (global)   | 21.8 µs   | ~9 ns, 0 allocations |
| self                | 45.0 µs   | ~9 ns, 0 allocations |
| via                 | unchanged | unchanged            |

Commit 2:
- Resolve grants lazily when via is present. Non-via grants are only read once a via grant matched, and destinations only for grants that match the viewer.
- via-mixed, 1,000 nodes: 69.0 µs → 11.6 µs.
- Policy that is only a via grant: about 5% slower (8.1 → 8.6 µs).
- Say you're happy to drop it if they'd rather keep this minimal.

Real-fleet check:
- Production export: 375 nodes, 245 users, real routes. All 62,850 peer pairs went from 84 s total on 0.29.4 to 0.55 ms.
- Separately, rewriting our acls as grants was our interim workaround, about 3.3×. That matches what the #3512 reporter found.

Tests:
- New subtest no_via_grant_returns_empty, plus BenchmarkViaRoutesForPeer.
- Existing via tests pass. policy/..., state, mapper and -race pass.
- Lint is clean.

Last line: Fixes #3512

title: [Feature] Limit on a number of nodes a user can register
body:
### Use case

All information is based on this code: https://github.com/YouSysAdmin/headscale/commit/23ac1f2bb5b394e5bd453011469fc8c660e4a42b

#### Configuration

```yaml
node:
  limits:
    # Maximum number of nodes a single user may own. 0 disables the limit (default).
    max_nodes_per_user: 0

    # Users the limit does not apply to. An entry matches a user's name or email.
    exempt_users: []

    # Whether nodes with an expired key count towards the limit.
    count_expired: true

    # Whether ephemeral nodes count towards the limit.
    count_ephemeral: true

    # When true, re-authenticating an existing node is also refused while the
    # user owns more nodes than the limit allows (e.g. after lowering it).
    enforce_on_reauth: false
```

With the defaults, behaviour is unchanged: no limit is applied and no extra locking happens.

#### Behaviour

- Tagged nodes never count. They are owned by their tags, not a user
  (tags XOR user ownership). This covers tagged pre-auth keys and interactive
  logins with `--advertise-tags`.

- Re-registration of an existing node is always allowed unless `enforce_on_reauth` is set.
  This covers restarts and key rotation. A node is never counted against itself.

- Converting a node to user-owned counts as a new node.
  This covers a tagged node moving to a user, and a machine re-registering for a different user.

- Pre-auth key path: `handleRegisterWithAuthKey` returns `RegisterResponse{Error: ...}` with HTTP 200, so the client shows the message as-is.

- Interactive path (web / CLI / OIDC): `HandleNodeFromAuthPath` resolves
  the pending auth request with the error. `waitForFollowup` now returns that
  error to the client.
  Previously a refused verdict fell through to a fresh
  `AuthURL`, which would have left the client in an endless login loop.
  Other refusals (reject, expiry) keep their existing behaviour.

- OIDC callback: renders a 403 page explaining the device limit.

- API / CLI auth register and nodes register map the error to 403 Forbidden instead of 500.

- Concurrency: registration is already serialized per machine key.
  While a limit is configured it is now also serialized per user, so two different
  machines of the same user cannot both pass the check before either is store. 
  The user lock is always taken after the machine-key lock.



### Description

Headscale has no way to limit how many nodes a single user can register.

When a registration would push a user over the limit, the node is refused and a Tailscale client is told why. Headscale returns `tailcfg.RegisterResponse.Error`, which the client surfaces as a user-visible error, so `tailscale up` and the GUI clients show:

```
backend error: node limit reached: user "alice" already has 1 node(s), the maximum allowed is 1, contact your administrator
```

### Contribution

- [ ] I can write the design doc for this feature
- [x] I can contribute this feature

### How can it be implemented?

I have a complete implementation of this feature: https://github.com/YouSysAdmin/headscale/commit/23ac1f2bb5b394e5bd453011469fc8c660e4a42b

I'm awaiting your approval to accept this into upstream. :)

title: hscontrol: arm ephemeral GC when a node registers with an auth key
body:
The ephemeral garbage collector was only armed when a long-poll session ended, or for every ephemeral node at startup. A client that registered and went away before its first long-poll reached `Connect`, for example a pod killed right after login, never ended a session, so no deletion timer was armed. The node then stayed until headscale restarted, well past `node.ephemeral.inactivity_timeout`.

Schedule the GC right after a successful auth-key registration. The existing `Cancel` in `serveLongPoll` stops the timer once the node connects. A timer that fires while a session is live is still skipped by the ActiveSessions check.

`TestEphemeralGCDoesNotDeleteReconnectedNode` now has longer `InactivityTimeout` set in order not to trigger the GC earlier than node reconnects

title: [Feature] Make headscale upgrade easier
body:
### Use case

Hi! I found #1526 and I'd love to help create APT repository for Headscale. However, I bumped into several problems and I'd need to know more about the current packages and upgrade process, which I find clunky at the moment.

### Description

## One minor version at a time – why?

Upgrade docs state (among other):

> Its required to update from one stable version to the next (e.g. 0.26.0 → 0.27.1 → 0.28.0) without skipping minor versions in between. You should always pick the latest available patch release.

Why is it not possible to jump two major versions at once? This might be a complication for APT repo, but still resolvable on user side with pinning. Does this limitation also include the `.deb` packages in GitHub Releases?

This is not natural for APT ecosystem. You can commonly upgrade the package by more than one minor version.

LLM suggests that headscale throws away old migrations (e.g. in commit `e90500e3`). Why? If we kept older migrations in the tree, they could be applied sequentially and it might make jumping more than one minor at once possible. And the migrations themselves shouldn't be too big.

Even if headscale dropped migrations in the past, it might be beneficial to stop doing that from now on. Or at the very least, define wider upgrade window than just two consecutive minor versions.

## Config changes

Headscale provides only `/etc/headscale/config.yml` as a configuration file. Therefore any package upgrade will resolve in a conflict. It's a common practice for Linux services to offer `conf.d` directory (e.g. `/etc/headscale/conf.d`) where users can drop overrides of default configuration. This could be done even with current YAML format (but we would have to be careful about deep dict merging strategy.

I understand that config can change in backwards-incompatible way. Even then, I'd love to have an option to just override it partially (using `conf.d`). If I want to be careful with upgrading, I can always use version pinning (which is reasonable and we might suggest it in the docs).

## Wrap up

I find the version restriction (one minor version bump only) the most strict and effectively blocking for a headscale APT repository. The config changes would be nice, but are not blocking (and may be resolved in another issue).

### Contribution

- [x] I can write the design doc for this feature
- [x] I can contribute this feature

### How can it be implemented?

I wrote I can implement this, but note that I'm not a Go developer. I'm experienced Python developer and I believe that I can make the changes necessary with the help of LLM, but I'd still need an experienced maintainer to review my changes and point me in the right direction.

Please, let me know what you think about the idea and what stands behind the decisions I dared to question here. If you agree with the general concept, I will draft more thorough design doc for your review, before we start making any code changes.
